why: NIOSSH reads an ssh-rsa key only once Citadel registers its RSA type, which the app never does: the app offers no RSA host-key algorithm, never meets an RSA host key and never stores the fingerprint of one. The Rust transport offers rsa-sha2-512/256 last and fingerprints an RSA key as ssh-keygen does (checked against ssh-keygen for every RSA case).

Fix: a host whose only host key is RSA. The app's NIOSSH client offers no RSA host-key algorithm, so the key exchange fails and the app can't connect at all; the Rust transport connects with rsa-sha2-512.

A PKCS#1 PEM or PKCS#8 key pasted without its .pub: SSHKeyFactory reads it (B29) and names its type, fingerprint and public line, then stores it as openssh-key-v1. This command asks the Rust side what inspect_private_key (the stored form's reader) says, and that reads openssh-key-v1 only, which is what every stored key is. Rust's import of these forms is moshpit_ssh::keyfile, cross-checked against the Swift import case by case in harness/keys_crosscheck.py (harness/key_divergences.json).

Fix: Citadel's detection, which SSHService.makeAuthMethod runs before every key sign-in, removes only "\n" before decoding the base64. A key with CRLF line endings (pasted or picked from Windows) or with indented lines fails it, though SSHKeyFactory.importKey (which drops all whitespace) imported it: the key is listed and can't sign in. The Rust side reads past any whitespace.

A key whose base64 was cut short. Citadel's detection reads only the public half at the front and calls it Ed25519; the Rust side reads the whole container and says it is broken. Moot in the app since d0f76d68: SSHKeyFactory.importKey refuses the same key (import-ed25519-truncated answers error on both sides), so it never reaches the detection before a sign-in.
The app refuses P-384 and P-521 keys at import (B29: Citadel signs with neither, so they could never sign in) and says so; inspect_private_key reads them, and the Rust transport signs with both.

A passphrase-protected key, asked without its passphrase: SSHKeyFactory.importKey needs it to read the key and refuses (the app asks for it and imports again, B29); inspect_private_key reads the public half, which openssh-key-v1 leaves in the clear, and reports the key encrypted.
